scoring_justification: Headline HEG sheet density values are compared to paper-reported values (Figure 6e) with a 15% relative tolerance, and a monotonic trend (sheet density must increase with compressive strain and decrease with tensile strain) is enforced as a hard gate.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference HEG sheet density values at specific a-axis strains
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Values extracted from Figure 6e of the paper (peak HEG sheet density vs strain) and the paper text stating ~1.1e13 cm⁻² at zero strain. Approximate digitised values: -1.78% ≈ 1.27e13, -0.89% ≈ 1.185e13, 0% = 1.1e13, 0.89% ≈ 1.015e13, 1.78% ≈ 9.3e12.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Digitised from published figure and cross-verified with text.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's own reported numbers, directly traceable to the published article.

outputs.description: CSV file with two columns: strain_percent (external a‑axis strain in percent, negative for compressive, positive for tensile) and sheet_density_cm2 (computed HEG sheet density in cm⁻²). The agent must include rows for at least the strain values -1.78, -0.89, 0.0, 0.89, 1.78. The checker will verify that the reported sheet density values are physically reasonable and follow the expected monotonic trend: sheet density must not increase as tensile strain increases (from 0 to positive strain) and must not decrease as compressive strain magnitude increases (from 0 to negative strain).

output_contract.notes: The checker additionally enforces a monotonicity requirement on the strain–density relationship; failure of this trend results in zero credit for this artifact.
